mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month decline in the federal funds rate signals an easing monetary cycle that compresses discount rates applied to equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the unemployment rate above 9.5% indicates labor market weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 returns as consumer spending and corporate earnings decline.
failure_condition: If the unemployment rate rises above 9.5% but the S&P 500 shows positive 20-day returns more than 40% of the time, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When GDP growth (GDPC1) decelerates while housing starts (HOUST) increase, it signals a mismatch in economic recovery, leading to negative S&P 500 returns as market participants anticipate a slowdown.
failure_condition: If GDPC1 growth is below 2% and HOUST exceeds 500K but the S&P 500 returns are positive over the next 60 days, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle, an increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) leads to higher borrowing costs, reducing corporate profitability and causing negative S&P 500 returns.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases by 25bps in one month
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS increases by 25bps but the S&P 500 shows positive 20-day returns more than 50% of the time, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) at a rate exceeding 3% annually signals inflationary pressures, leading to negative S&P 500 returns as the Federal Reserve is expected to tighten monetary policy.
failure_condition: If CPIAUCSL increases by more than 3% annually but the S&P 500 returns are positive over the next 20 days, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% over three months signals supply chain disruptions, leading to negative S&P 500 returns as corporate earnings are negatively impacted.
failure_condition: If INDPRO declines by more than 2% over three months but the S&P 500 returns are positive over the next 60 days, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When payroll employment (PAYEMS) increases but retail sales (RSAFS) decline, it indicates weak consumer demand, leading to negative S&P 500 returns as businesses face reduced revenues.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by 100K but RSAFS declines by 1%
failure_condition: If PAYEMS increases by 100K and RSAFS declines by 1% but the S&P 500 returns are positive over the next 20 days, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: During an economic expansion, a low unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 5% signals a strong labor market, leading to positive S&P 500 returns as consumer spending and corporate earnings increase.
failure_condition: If UNRATE falls below 5% but the S&P 500 returns are negative over the next 60 days, the hypothesis is rejected.
